cues.en: Good morning, everyone. My name is Felina.
cues.zh: 大家早上好。我叫 Felina。

cues.en: I'm on Twitter as well. My Twitter handle is just my first name, very easy. So if you wanna share something about my talk, please mention me so I can see what was going on in the room while I was talking.
cues.zh: 我也在 Twitter 上。我的 Twitter 用户名就是我的名，很简单。如果你想分享关于我这场演讲的内容，请 @ 我，这样我在讲的时候也能看到现场在聊什么。

cues.en: My talk today is about how to teach programming,
cues.zh: 我今天的演讲主题是如何教编程，

cues.en: and if teaching at the university has taught me anything,
cues.zh: 如果说在大学教书让我学到了什么，

cues.en: it is that early morning lectures really need audience participation.
cues.zh: 那就是清晨的讲座真的需要观众参与。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: let's go. Who knows who said this? Everyone should learn programming. Anyone knows who said this?
cues.zh: 我们开始吧。谁知道这句话是谁说的？“每个人都应该学编程。”有人知道是谁说的吗？

cues.en: Bill Gates.
cues.zh: Bill Gates。

cues.en: Other guesses?
cues.zh: 还有其他猜测吗？

cues.en: Alan Kay. Nice one.
cues.zh: Alan Kay。不错。

cues.en: Pepper. Same or Pepper. Nice nice.
cues.zh: Pepper。Same 还是 Pepper。好好好。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: it's sort of all correct because it's every programmer ever.
cues.zh: 这些答案某种程度上都算对，因为说这话的是每个程序员。

cues.en: We all love programming,
cues.zh: 我们都热爱编程，

cues.en: right? We are all like, oh, programming is the best, so everyone should learn it. But of course, this
cues.zh: 对吧？我们都觉得，哦，编程最棒了，所以每个人都该学。但当然，这

cues.en: puts us in a sort of interesting position because many people then actually start to teach programming. So many people that are programmers, they run a code club or they teach their own children or friends over their children, but
cues.zh: 让我们处在一个有点有趣的位置，因为很多人随后真的开始教编程。很多程序员会办代码俱乐部，或者教自己的孩子、朋友或朋友的孩子，但

cues.en: how actually to teach programming? Because most people don't really know how to teach programming. So that is the topic of my talk today,
cues.zh: 到底该怎么教编程？因为大多数人其实并不知道怎么教编程。所以这就是我今天演讲的主题，

cues.en: how to teach programming.
cues.zh: 如何教编程。

cues.en: But before we go into this, I'm not an educator,
cues.zh: 但在进入正题之前，先说明，我不是教育工作者，

cues.en: so I want to take you through the story of how I came to think about how to teach programming. And for that, we have to go back to the year 2008,
cues.zh: 所以我想带大家回顾一下，我是怎么开始思考如何教编程的。为此，我们得回到 2008 年，

cues.en: when I started to work on my PhD research at Delft University in The Netherlands.
cues.zh: 那时我开始在荷兰的代尔夫特理工大学做博士研究。

cues.en: My research was about how to create a DSL,
cues.zh: 我的研究是关于如何创建一种 DSL，

cues.en: a domain specific language for finance.
cues.zh: 一种面向金融领域的领域特定语言。

cues.en: So me and my supervisor, we envisioned something like this, A textual programming language in which non programmers
cues.zh: 我和我的导师设想的是这样的东西：一种文本编程语言，让非程序员

cues.en: could express themselves
cues.zh: 能够表达自己

cues.en: so that they didn't need a programmer for anything. So they could create their own little apps and programs to empower themselves to run their own companies in a more efficient or interesting way.
cues.zh: 这样他们做任何事都不需要程序员。他们可以自己创建小应用和程序，赋能自己以更高效或更有趣的方式经营自己的公司。

cues.en: Because of course, there aren't enough programmers to build everything, so it's very good if we can empower users to build their own programs.
cues.zh: 因为当然，没有足够的程序员来构建所有东西，所以如果我们能赋能用户构建自己的程序，那非常好。

cues.en: I started this PhD project with an internship at an insurance company, and in that insurance company, there worked many non programmers.
cues.zh: 我以在一家保险公司的实习开始了这个博士项目，那家保险公司里有很多非程序员在工作。

cues.en: So in my mind, I was like, oh, all those people, they really need my help. They're like, help us, Selena. We need you. We need your domain specific language to help us with creating stuff on the computer.
cues.zh: 所以我心里想，哦，所有那些人，他们真的需要我的帮助。他们会说，帮帮我们吧，Selena。我们需要你。我们需要你的领域特定语言来帮我们在电脑上创建东西。

cues.en: But it wasn't anything like that. I was like, hello. Can I help you with making programs? And they're like, yeah, we're fine, actually.
cues.zh: 但根本不是那样。我说，你好。我能帮你们做程序吗？他们说，是啊，其实我们挺好的。

cues.en: We don't need your help. We are already programming.
cues.zh: 我们不需要你的帮助。我们已经在编程了。

cues.en: All those people, the non programmers,
cues.zh: 所有那些人，那些非程序员，

cues.en: they were actually already programming within their company if they needed anything like a budget or a planning.
cues.zh: 如果他们需要预算或规划之类的东西，他们其实已经在公司内部编程了。

cues.en: They didn't need a domain specific language. They didn't need the they didn't need the IT department. They were just programming it themselves.
cues.zh: 他们不需要领域特定语言。他们不需要，他们不需要 IT 部门。他们只是自己编程搞定。

cues.en: But they weren't programming in a traditional programming language,
cues.zh: 但他们用的不是传统的编程语言，

cues.en: they were programming in spreadsheets.
cues.zh: 而是用电子表格在编程。

cues.en: The whole insurance company, and I saw many other companies after that,
cues.zh: 整家保险公司——后来我也在很多其他公司见识过——

cues.en: was just ran by spreadsheets. Everyone was building spreadsheets for everything, so they were sort of fine. I went back to my supervisor, I said, I don't think they need a DSL in finance.
cues.zh: 完全就是靠电子表格运转的。大家做什么都在建电子表格，其实过得挺滋润。我回去跟导师说：我觉得金融领域根本不需要 DSL。

cues.en: They have a DSL in finance.
cues.zh: 金融领域早就有 DSL 了。

cues.en: It's Excel.
cues.zh: 那就是 Excel。

cues.en: It is just an amazing programming language. I really say this without any irony.
cues.zh: 它真是一门极其出色的编程语言，我这么说绝无半点讽刺。

cues.en: Spreadsheets are the best programming language that has ever existed in the history of programming languages, really. Thank
cues.zh: 电子表格真的是编程语言史上最棒的语言，真心的。谢……

cues.en: you.
cues.zh: ……谢大家。

cues.en: I mean, it is such a good programming language that people don't know their programming.
cues.zh: 我是说，它好到大家甚至都没意识到自己是在编程。

cues.en: Let that sink in. Hey, imagine this happening for Java. It's hey, I installed Eclipse on my laptop. It was super easy in Windows,
cues.zh: 仔细品品。想象一下如果这发生在 Java 身上：“嘿，我在笔记本上装了 Eclipse，在 Windows 上特别好装，

cues.en: and then I opened it up, and I immediately knew what to do, and I built this budget sheet.
cues.zh: 然后我一打开，立马就知道该怎么搞，顺手就做了张预算表。”

cues.en: See how ridiculous this sounds for any programming language? You cannot just jump into a programming language. You cannot even get it to work often.
cues.zh: 对任何编程语言来说，这话听着有多荒谬？你不可能随便就能上手一门编程语言，很多时候甚至连跑都跑不起来。

cues.en: But for Excel, it works like that. You just jump in and start and add some data, and you know what to do because the interface is really intuitive.
cues.zh: 但 Excel 就是可以。你直接打开就能上手填数据，因为界面非常直观，你自然就知道该怎么操作。

cues.en: So my story at that point became spreadsheets are code. Spreadsheets are a programming language, and this is a talk, actually, a similar talk I did at Changeloop a bunch of years ago.
cues.zh: 所以那时我的观点就变成了：电子表格就是代码，电子表格就是编程语言。其实几年前我在 Changeloop 也做过类似的演讲。

cues.en: So I went on to go to conferences because I I really like speaking at conferences. So I went to conferences. I was like, hello, everyone. Spreadsheets are cool. I want to share this happy news with all of you.
cues.zh: 于是我就去参加各种会议，因为我真的很喜欢在会议上演讲。所以我就去了会议。我说，大家好。电子表格很酷。我想和你们分享这个好消息。

cues.en: But I wasn't so happy because people will be like, that's not real programming.
cues.zh: 但我没那么开心，因为人们会说，那不算真正的编程。

cues.en: And I was like, wait. Wait. Wait. Wait. Wait. Okay. I understand you're a bit skeptic, but I made a Turing machine in spreadsheets
cues.zh: 我就想，等等。等等。等等。等等。等等。好吧。我理解你们有点怀疑，但我在电子表格里做了一个图灵机

cues.en: using only formulas.
cues.zh: 只用公式做的。

cues.en: This must convince you that it is a programming language.
cues.zh: 这总该说服你们它是一种编程语言了吧。

cues.en: Right? This is my Turing machine made with spreadsheet formulas only. So all the rows are different versions
cues.zh: 对吧？这是我的图灵机，只用电子表格公式做的。每一行都是纸带的不同版本

cues.en: of the tape and the head moves over it with conditional formatting. Super cool. I present to you, spreadsheets are programming languages.
cues.zh: 读写头通过条件格式在纸带上移动。超酷。我向你们展示，电子表格就是编程语言。

cues.en: Thank you for that, but the people remained unconvinced.
cues.zh: 谢谢你们，但人们仍然不信服。

cues.en: They were, yeah, okay, but it's not real programming because it doesn't have this or it doesn't have that or too many people can use it.
cues.zh: 他们说，好吧好吧，但那不算真正的编程，因为它没有这个，或者没有那个，或者太多人都能用它。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: this was a serious argument people used. It cannot be programming because everyone understands it. Really?
cues.zh: 这是人们真的用过的严肃论点。它不可能是编程，因为每个人都能看懂它。真的吗？

cues.en: Wait, what?
cues.zh: 等等，什么？

cues.en: So it sort of went on like this, and and after a while, I mean, it really dragged me down.
cues.zh: 事情就这样持续下去，过了一阵子，我是说，这真的让我很沮丧。

cues.en: Who who in the audience has a PhD or is working on a PhD?
cues.zh: 观众里谁有博士学位，或者正在读博士？

cues.en: Quite a bunch. Yeah. So you know this, but I guess other people also understand this, that you and your topic sort of become this one thing. And if people say your topic isn't real or worthy, then, you know, you get sadder
cues.zh: 还挺多的。是的。所以你们知道这种感觉，但我想其他人也懂，就是你和你的课题某种程度上变成了同一件事。如果人们说你的课题不是真的或者不值得，那你知道，你会越来越难过

cues.en: and sadder
cues.zh: 越来越

cues.en: and sadder, really. I was... At the end of my PhD, I was I was ready to call it quits with this researcher. I was just I was just super sad, and then it it really drags you down if people say your topic isn't important.
cues.zh: 越来越难过，真的。我在……博士快结束的时候，我准备放弃做研究者了。我就是，我就是特别难过，而当人们说你的课题不重要时，真的会把你拖垮。

cues.en: And at this point in time, I thought, okay, this is just this is just life.
cues.zh: 那时我想，好吧，这就是生活，这就是生活。

cues.en: Apparently,
cues.zh: 显然，

cues.en: if adults hang out with each other, they will just call each other's work shit. That's just normal.
cues.zh: 如果成年人一起玩，他们就会说彼此的工作是狗屎。这很正常。

cues.en: Little did I know. I thought maybe I should just toughen up. I should just have a bigger, thicker skin because people would just be mean to me. It wasn't until way later in 2015
cues.zh: 我完全没想到。我以为自己该坚强点，脸皮厚点，因为人们就是会对我刻薄；直到很久之后的2015年

cues.en: actually
cues.zh: 其实

cues.en: when I joined a running group
cues.zh: 我加入一个跑团之后

cues.en: that I figured out that people can be nice to each other.
cues.zh: 我才发现人们可以彼此友善。

cues.en: This is what it took really.
cues.zh: 真的，我花了这么久才明白。

cues.en: So I really like running and I joined this running group, but I'm not a very quick runner. So my best half marathon is two hours,
cues.zh: 我很喜欢跑步，加入了这个跑团，但我跑得不快。我半马最好成绩是两小时，

cues.en: and that's also the world's record for the full marathon. So I'm like twice as slow. And there were people in my running group where I did a half marathon in two hours, and they do half marathon in like one hour ten.
cues.zh: 这也是全马的世界纪录。所以我差不多慢了一倍。我跑团里有些人，我半马跑两小时，他们半马跑一小时十分。

cues.en: So they were way better than me. But no one in this group said,
cues.zh: 他们比我强多了。但跑团里没人说：

cues.en: you're not a real runner. Oh, a half marathon takes you two hours. That's not real running.
cues.zh: “你不是真正的跑者。半马要跑两小时，那不算真正的跑步。”

cues.en: People will never say that. I mean, if you put the shoes on, you're a runner. People wouldn't say things like,
cues.zh: 人们绝不会这么说。我是说，穿上鞋，你就是跑者。没人会说这种话：

cues.en: oh, you have Adidas shoes,
cues.zh: “哦，你穿 Adidas 鞋，”

cues.en: but they have security vulnerabilities.
cues.zh: “但它有安全漏洞。”

cues.en: You cannot run on them.
cues.zh: “你不能穿它跑步。”

cues.en: No one talks shit about each other's gear. I mean, whatever shoes you wear, you can go barefoot, you can have a shirt or a shirt, it doesn't matter. No one is mean about anything.
cues.zh: 没人贬低彼此的装备。我是说，不管你穿什么鞋，光脚也行，穿不穿上衣都行，无所谓。没人会刻薄。

cues.en: It's
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: so weird.
cues.zh: 太奇怪了。

cues.en: It's it's even... It's not even that we're inclusive.
cues.zh: 甚至……甚至都算不上是包容。

cues.en: We we are we are terrible. Is anyone in the audience a runner?
cues.zh: 我们……我们简直太可怕了。观众席里有跑步的吗？

cues.en: A bunch? Yeah? So so we are terrible. We want everyone to be runners. We we almost go door to door like Jehovah's Witnesses, ding dong, hello, have you heard the happy news about running? It will really change your life, and we will make you such a happier person. We are like that. If I see you running through the bus, I'll be like, oh, do you like running? Do you wanna go on a race together? What's your personal record? We are the worst. I mean, we are the best. We are such an inclusive
cues.zh: 挺多？是吧？所以我们真的很可怕。我们巴不得所有人都在跑步。我们简直像耶和华见证人一样挨家挨户敲门：“叮咚，你好，你听说过跑步的福音吗？它真的能改变你的生活，让你变成一个更快乐的人。”我们就是这种人。如果我看到你在追公交，我就会问：“噢，你喜欢跑步吗？要不要一起去跑个比赛？你个人最好成绩是多少？”我们太招人烦了。我是说，我们太棒了。我们是一个超级包容的

cues.en: community.
cues.zh: 社群。

cues.en: Yeah. It is just amazing, and it's not just running.
cues.zh: 没错。这真的很神奇，而且不仅跑步是这样。

cues.en: It's also knitting. I really like knitting. I knitted a lot when I was a teenager, and I went to university, and I started to stop knitting.
cues.zh: 织毛衣也是。我特别喜欢织毛衣。我十几岁的时候经常织，后来上了大学，就慢慢不织了。

cues.en: And then I came back to knitting in 2016,
cues.zh: 然后在 2016 年，我又重新捡起了编织，

cues.en: and I went to a knitting meetup.
cues.zh: 还去参加了一场织毛衣的聚会。

cues.en: However, times had changed in the knitting community
cues.zh: 然而，编织圈的时代早就变了，

cues.en: because when I was a teenager, everyone used these old fashioned straight long needles that you might remember from people knitting
cues.zh: 因为我年轻的时候，大家用的都是那种老式长直针，就是你们记忆中人们

cues.en: in the old days. But now, everyone has circular needles.
cues.zh: 过去织毛衣用的那种。但现在，人人都在用环形针。

cues.en: They are one needle, they are round. So I come to this meetup with my old fashioned straight needles, and everyone has these circular needles.
cues.zh: 它们是连成一体的圆环针。所以当我拿着老式长直针来到聚会，发现大家用的都是环形针。

cues.en: So I'm like, oh, shit. This is going to be not real knitting. Beep, beep, I'm going go home. This will be terrible. But it wasn't like that. They were like, no, of course, it doesn't matter. We can teach you if you want to, but if you don't want to learn and you want to stay with your old fashioned needles, that's fine too.
cues.zh: 我心里就想：“卧槽。他们肯定觉得我这不算真正的编织。溜了溜了，我要回家，太糟糕了。”但事实并非如此。他们说：“没事，这当然无所谓。你想学的话我们可以教你；但如果你不想学，想继续用老式长针，也完全没问题。”

cues.en: Wow.
cues.zh: 哇。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: then I realized
cues.zh: 后来我意识到

cues.en: that there were other people that were also nice and inclusive, and that it didn't have to be that not real programming vibe.
cues.zh: 原来还有其他人也很友善、包容，编程不一定非得是那种“不算真正编程”的氛围。

cues.en: And actually, it's getting even better because this year,
cues.zh: 而且，事情其实变得更好了，因为今年

cues.en: there's someone,
cues.zh: 有一位

cues.en: a talk tomorrow by Laura Shank, she has a talk about CSS
cues.zh: Laura Shank 明天有一场关于 CSS

cues.en: being a programming language.
cues.zh: 是编程语言的演讲。

cues.en: I was like, wow. People are so inclusive in so many communities, like Strange Loop and Knitting and Running.
cues.zh: 我当时想，哇，很多社区都特别包容，比如 Strange Loop、编织和跑步社区。

cues.en: It can actually be different. So definitely be sure to check out this talk tomorrow.
cues.zh: 其实完全可以不一样。所以明天一定要去听听这场演讲。

cues.en: But let's go back to 2013. It's
cues.zh: 不过我们回到 2013 年。当时是

cues.en: 2013 again.
cues.zh: 又一个 2013 年。

cues.en: I am sad.
cues.zh: 我很难过。

cues.en: I have just graduated my PhD,
cues.zh: 我刚刚读完博士，

cues.en: and I went on a job interview at Delft University where I also did my PhD,
cues.zh: 然后去 Delft University 面试，我也是在那里读的博士，

cues.en: and in that job interview, I blatantly lied about being super excited about spreadsheets because it was such a good research idea to do stuff with spreadsheets, and they fell for the lie, so now I was hired.
cues.zh: 面试时，我厚着脸皮谎称自己对电子表格超级感兴趣，因为用电子表格做研究是个特别好的想法，而他们居然信了，所以我就被录用了。

cues.en: I had to work on spreadsheets
cues.zh: 我的工作是研究电子表格

cues.en: with two PhD students and a postdoc,
cues.zh: 和两名博士生、一名博士后一起，

cues.en: but I wasn't really feeling it. I mean, it's funny now, but it was actually kind
cues.zh: 但我其实完全提不起劲。现在说起来挺好笑，但当时真的有点

cues.en: of sad because on the one hand side, I really wanted to work on this because I still believe it's a very, very valuable thing to work on,
cues.zh: 难过，因为一方面，我确实很想做这件事，因为我到现在仍然相信这是非常、非常有价值的研究方向，

cues.en: but on the other hand, it just... It had worn me out. So I was super, super sad.
cues.zh: 但另一方面，这件事已经把我耗尽了。所以我当时特别特别难过。

cues.en: By a total lifesaving coincidence,
cues.zh: 就在这时，一个完全救命的巧合发生了，

cues.en: at this point in time, I ran into a bunch of kids in the community center that needed a programming teacher.
cues.zh: 我在社区中心遇到了一群孩子，他们需要一位编程老师。

cues.en: So I was like, okay, I will teach children on Saturdays programming because at least I will be
cues.zh: 所以我当时想，好吧，我周六教孩子们编程，这样至少周六的生活也算有意义。

cues.zh: 这是因为你进行了一种叫做“组块”（chunking）的操作。你在大脑中压缩了信息量，处理起来就变得极其轻松。

cues.en: If
cues.zh: 如果

cues.en: I would really have bet a
cues.zh: 我真跟你打赌

cues.en: thousand dollars with you, and you're actually trying to remember this, what happens is you feel your working memory get overloaded,
cues.zh: 赌上一千美元，而你也真的努力去记，结果就会是：你会感到工作记忆过载了，

cues.en: right? You really want to remember this, oh, it's a circle with a dot and a steak and a sigma reverse, and there's diamonds and a big C.
cues.zh: 对吧？你拼命想记住：哦，这是一个带点的圆圈、一根小棍、一个反向的 sigma，还有几个菱形和一个大写的 C。

cues.en: It doesn't fit in your brain.
cues.zh: 你的脑子根本装不下。

cues.en: You experience this fullness almost, and that fullness is called cognitive load. So once your working memory is too full, you experience cognitive load,
cues.zh: 你几乎会感受到一种“满载感”，而这种满载感就叫做认知负荷。一旦工作记忆过满，你就会感受到认知负荷，

cues.en: and this helps us understand
cues.zh: 这有助于我们理解

cues.en: why this first group did so much better than the second group,
cues.zh: 为什么第一组的表现比第二组好得多，

cues.en: because in the second group, the cognitive load was too high.
cues.zh: 因为在第二组中，认知负荷太高了。

cues.en: So what happened is the children were solving the problems.
cues.zh: 当时的情况是，孩子们确实在做题。

cues.en: They succeeded in solving them, but there was no cognitive
cues.zh: 他们成功解出了题目，但大脑中已经没有多余的

cues.en: load room left in their brain to actually remember and reflect what they were doing. So they didn't memorize everything after having solved the problems.
cues.zh: 认知空间来真正记住和反思自己在做什么。所以做完题后，他们什么都没记住。

cues.en: And the biggest thing, I think, to take away from Kirchner's and Sweller's work is you don't become an expert by doing expert things.
cues.zh: 我认为从 Kirchner 和 Sweller 的研究中得到的最大启发是：你不会因为做专家做的事就成为专家。

cues.en: Like with the soccer example,
cues.zh: 就像足球的例子一样，

cues.en: you don't
cues.zh: 你不会

cues.en: practice a soccer match. If you're training for a marathon, you don't do a marathon every day. That's a terrible
cues.zh: 靠踢整场比赛来训练。如果你在备战马拉松，你也不会每天都跑个马拉松。那简直是

cues.en: idea.
cues.zh: 馊主意。

cues.en: But for problem solving, it makes so much sense,
cues.zh: 但在解决问题这件事上，大家却觉得顺理成章，

cues.en: and I've heard many people in different contexts say this very often, yeah, but I want children to be problem solvers,
cues.zh: 我经常在各种场合听很多人这么说：“对啊，但我希望孩子们成为问题的解决者，

cues.en: so they should solve problems.
cues.zh: 所以他们就该去解决问题。”

cues.en: But sadly, it doesn't work like that. If you want children to be good problem solvers,
cues.zh: 但遗憾的是，事实并非如此。如果你想让孩子们善于解决问题，

cues.en: you need to make sure they have enough problem solving chunks in their brain that they can rely on.
cues.zh: 你得确保他们脑子里有足够多可供依赖的“问题解决组块”。

cues.en: So my big strategy from my research plan is to start a fight.
cues.zh: 所以我的研究计划的核心策略是挑起一场“争论”。

cues.en: I mean, a nice fight. Emphatic go to the debate because I want to talk about these two sides of programming education,
cues.zh: 我是指良性的争论。有力地展开辩论，因为我想探讨编程教育的这两面，

cues.en: because that side
cues.zh: 因为那一面

cues.en: has been
cues.zh: 一直被

cues.en: overemphasized
cues.zh: 过度强调了，

cues.en: partly because of the involvement and historical
cues.zh: 部分是由于 Seymour Papert 的参与和历史

cues.en: background of Seymour Paperts. Everyone is talking about this type of teaching in programming.
cues.zh: 背景。大家都在谈论编程中的这种教学方式。

cues.en: So I want to talk about this type of teaching. How would direct instruction
cues.zh: 所以我想聊聊另一种教学方式。直接教学法

cues.en: look like for programming?
cues.zh: 在编程中会是什么样子？

cues.en: What could we do if we're really focused on explaining children, students the basics of programming and make sure that they practice a lot in the right way?
cues.zh: 如果我们真正专注于向儿童、学生讲解编程基础，并确保他们以正确的方式进行大量练习，我们能做些什么？

cues.en: So one of the researches I've done in this direction, and I am very, very excited about, is we've been experimenting
cues.zh: 在这个方向上，我做过的一项让我非常非常兴奋的研究，就是我们一直在尝试

cues.en: with having children read source code aloud.
cues.zh: 让孩子们大声朗读源代码。

cues.en: Remember this.
cues.zh: 记住这一点。

cues.en: Remember
cues.zh: 记住

cues.en: how much it matters how something sounds in your brain for you to interpret the meaning.
cues.zh: 一句话在脑海里的读音，对你理解它的含义有多么重要。

cues.en: We asked a bunch of children
cues.zh: 我们找了一群孩子，

cues.en: to read some Python aloud,
cues.zh: 让他们大声朗读一些 Python 代码，

cues.en: just a snippet like this.
cues.zh: 就像这样的一小段。

cues.en: X equals signs five. What do you think this says children?
cues.zh: X 等号 5。“孩子们，你们觉得这念什么？”

cues.en: X is five.
X equals five.
cues.zh: “X 等于 5。”

cues.en: X gets five. Set x to five. Assign five to x.
cues.zh: “X 取 5。”“设 X 为 5。”“把 5 赋给 X。”

cues.en: It all makes sense,
cues.zh: 这些都说得通，

cues.en: but there's no consistent model for how people say this.
cues.zh: 但大家念它的方式并没有统一的认知模式。

cues.en: The interesting thing about this study
cues.zh: 这项研究有趣的地方在于，

cues.en: is we didn't do it with random kids, we did it with Dutch kids.
cues.zh: 我们并不是随便找的孩子，找的是荷兰的孩子。

cues.en: And we didn't really anticipate them. Dutch kids are in my country, so we didn't really anticipate this would have an effect,
cues.zh: 我们当时并没预料到……荷兰孩子就在我们国家，所以我们没料到这会有什么影响，

cues.en: but a very, very, very interesting thing happened that we didn't think of.
cues.zh: 但发生了一件我们完全没想到的、非常非常有趣的事。

cues.en: This letter,
cues.zh: 这个字母，

cues.en: in English,
cues.zh: 在英语里，

cues.en: of course, is the I,
cues.zh: 当然念作 I（/aɪ/），

cues.en: as in Thai.
cues.zh: 就像 Thai 里的读音。

cues.en: In Dutch, my native language, it is not pronounced I, it is pronounced I,
cues.zh: 但在我的母语荷兰语里，它不念 I，而是念作 /iː/，

cues.en: as in creep.
cues.zh: 就像 creep 里的读音。

cues.en: So we had kids that read this code snippet as follows. They said, for I in range,
cues.zh: 于是我们发现，有些孩子是这么读这段代码的：他们念“for I in range”，

cues.en: print e.
cues.zh: 然后是“print /iː/”。

cues.en: Within the same code snippet.
cues.zh: 就在同一段代码里。

cues.en: And that, of course, raises the question,
cues.zh: 这当然就引出了一个问题：

cues.en: do they really, in their subconscious mind, have realized it's the same variable?
cues.zh: 在他们的潜意识里，真的意识到这是同一个变量了吗？

cues.en: Tear or tear, probably
cues.zh: 就像多音字 tear 一样，很可能

cues.en: they haven't really got it connected well that it's the same variable.
cues.zh: 他们并没有真正把它们关联起来，意识到这其实是同一个变量。

cues.en: So this is something we should explore, and it makes sense to say it like this because
cues.zh: 所以这是个值得我们探讨的现象，而且这么读也合情合理，因为

cues.en: Dutch, these are 12 year olds. Dutch 12 year olds know some English. So for the first sentence, their brain goes into English mode. For eye in range.
cues.zh: 荷兰——这些都是 12 岁的孩子，荷兰的 12 岁孩子懂一些英语。所以在读第一句时，他们的大脑切换到了英语模式：“for I in range”。

cues.en: But then for the next one, they're like, oh, so what does it do with the eye? Detailed reading, print e.
cues.zh: 但到了下一个，他们就会说，哦，那它对 i 做什么？细读，print e。

cues.en: So it makes sense that you have these two modes of reading if you're a Dutch kid, but it will hamper
cues.zh: 所以如果你是荷兰孩子，有这两种阅读模式说得通，但这会妨碍

cues.en: your... The readability
cues.zh: 你的……可读性

cues.en: of source code if you don't explicitly practice this.
cues.zh: 源代码的可读性，如果你不刻意练习这一点。

cues.en: So we actually did a study in which we told children how to read code aloud.
cues.zh: 所以我们真的做了一项研究，教孩子们如何大声读代码。

cues.en: So really, in a classroom setting, repeat this after me, children, for I in range,
cues.zh: 所以在课堂上，孩子们，跟我念：for I in range，

cues.en: round open bracket four,
cues.zh: 圆左括号，四，

cues.en: round closing bracket colon.
cues.zh: 圆右括号，冒号。

cues.en: We really had to practice the syntax aloud,
cues.zh: 我们真的必须大声练习语法，

cues.en: and this works.
cues.zh: 而这有效。

cues.en: So the group that red code aloud every week did better on a syntax test after this course, so they were better able to remember syntax.
cues.zh: 所以每周大声读代码的那组，在这门课后语法测试中表现更好，也更能记住语法。

cues.en: And this is the paper if you want to read the paper.
cues.zh: 这是那篇论文，如果你想读的话。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: everyone is angry with me.
cues.zh: 所有人都生我的气。

cues.en: So my life has not really gotten any better because people in programming are really upset about this. The first time we submitted this paper, it was actually rejected, and one of the reviewers said,
cues.zh: 所以我的生活并没有真正变好，因为编程圈的人对此非常不满。我们第一次提交这篇论文时，它其实被拒了，其中一位审稿人说，

cues.en: this paper doesn't make sense because programming
cues.zh: 这篇论文说不通，因为编程

cues.en: is not about syntax.
cues.zh: 不在于语法。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: what is it about, reviewer two?
cues.zh: 那它到底关于什么，二号审稿人？

cues.en: I don't know.
cues.zh: 我不知道。

cues.en: So... And again, this is this different level. This is
cues.zh: 所以……再说一次，这是另一个层次。这是

cues.en: break the rules, and this is Python. Of course, programming is not about syntax, but also it is because you need syntax
cues.zh: 打破规则，而这是 Python。当然，编程不在于语法，但也不全是，因为你需要语法

cues.en: to be able to make anything.
cues.zh: 才能做出任何东西。

cues.en: But how upset programming
cues.zh: 但编程界有多不满，

cues.en: is, is nothing compared
cues.zh: 根本不算什么，比起

cues.en: to how upset elementary school teachers are with this result.
cues.zh: 小学老师对这个结果有多不满。

cues.en: If I go to teaching conferences and I talk about this, they're like,
cues.zh: 如果我去参加教学会议谈到这个，他们会说，

cues.en: okay, lady, so it is 2019,
cues.zh: 好了，女士，现在都2019年了，

cues.en: and you people in programming,
cues.zh: 你们搞编程的人，

cues.en: you have figured out that
cues.zh: 总算搞明白了

cues.en: making children read stuff aloud
cues.zh: 让孩子大声朗读

cues.en: actually helps their understanding of things.
cues.zh: 其实有助于他们理解东西。

cues.en: Slow clap.
cues.zh: 慢慢鼓掌。

cues.en: We are so impressed.
cues.zh: 我们真是太佩服了。

cues.en: Thank
cues.zh: 谢谢

cues.en: you for this amazing work, doctor Hermann.
cues.zh: 你这了不起的工作，Hermann博士。

cues.en: They know this in education. They know it really, really well. We are the fools here.
cues.zh: 教育界早就知道这个了。他们非常非常清楚。我们才是傻子。

cues.en: They know this, not even just for reading language, but also for math. How do you learn the tables of multiplication?
cues.zh: 他们知道这个，不只是读语言，数学也一样。你怎么学乘法表？

cues.en: One times four is four. Two times four is eight. How often have you practiced that? Hundreds of times. It just makes so much sense, but as far as we know, we are the first ones to actually have explored this for programming syntax with unsurprising results.
cues.zh: 一四得四。二四得八。你练过多少遍？几百遍。这太合理了，但据我们所知，我们是第一批真正在编程语法上探索这个的人，结果不出所料。

cues.en: So that is a thing that works.
cues.zh: 所以这招是管用的。

cues.en: Another thing,
cues.zh: 另一件事，

cues.en: revolutionary
cues.zh: 革命性的

cues.en: idea,
cues.zh: 想法，

cues.en: is you can actually tell students how to solve problems.
cues.zh: 就是你可以直接告诉学生怎么解决问题。

cues.en: That also works really well. I found this amazing paper from 1992.
cues.zh: 这也很管用。我找到了一篇1992年的精彩论文。

cues.en: Some people in the audience might have not been born, so it is very old,
cues.zh: 有些观众可能还没出生，所以它很老了，

cues.en: and this paper is called The Case for Case Studies in Pascal. It's also easy to find on the Internet if you want to check it out. What did they do in this study? These were high school children.
cues.zh: 这篇论文叫《The Case for Case Studies in Pascal》。网上也很容易找到，想看去查。他们在这项研究里做了什么？研究对象是高中生。

cues.en: They had three groups. The first group of children wrote their own code as a solution to a problem,
cues.zh: 他们分了三组。第一组孩子自己写代码作为问题的解答，

cues.en: and then after they've written the code, they got the solution that an expert would write
cues.zh: 写完代码后，他们拿到了专家会写的解答

cues.en: as an inspiration to learn from, first group.
cues.zh: 作为学习灵感，这是第一组。

cues.en: Second group, same
cues.zh: 第二组，同样

cues.en: setup almost. They wrote their own code, then they got expert code to read, but also they got an explanation.
cues.zh: 设置得差不多了。他们写了自己的代码，然后拿到了专家代码来阅读，但也得到了讲解。

cues.en: So next to the code they were reading, an expert would have said, well, here I use a for loop, and then I use a variable. This is the steps that I take, this is why.
cues.zh: 所以在他们阅读的代码旁边，专家会说，这里我用了一个 for 循环，然后我用了一个变量。这是我采取的步骤，这是为什么。

cues.en: Then there was also a third group. They did not write any code
cues.zh: 然后还有第三组。他们在整个课程中

cues.en: in the entire class.
cues.zh: 没有写任何代码。

cues.en: The only thing they did is they studied expert code
cues.zh: 他们唯一做的就是学习专家代码，

cues.en: with accompanying explanation
cues.zh: 附带讲解，

cues.en: of how you create code.
cues.zh: 讲解的是如何创建代码。

cues.en: So these are the three groups. Write and read code, write and read code plus an explanation,
cues.zh: 所以这就是三组。写代码和读代码，写代码和读代码加讲解，

cues.en: just reading code plus an explanation.
cues.zh: 只是读代码加讲解。

cues.en: The teachers
cues.zh: 老师们

cues.en: very much preferred, these were programming teachers, the first condition. They said, first they have to solve the problem, and maybe then we give them the code but not the explanation.
cues.zh: 非常偏好，这些是编程老师，第一种条件。他们说，首先他们得解决问题，也许然后我们给他们代码但不给讲解。

cues.en: But who actually did better?
cues.zh: 但谁实际上做得更好？

cues.en: The second and the third group did equally well.
cues.zh: 第二组和第三组做得一样好。

cues.en: So the group writing the code and reading code plus explanation did as good as the group that was just reading code plus an explanation, and the first group did worse.
cues.zh: 所以写代码和读代码加讲解的那组，和只是读代码加讲解的那组做得一样好，而第一组做得更差。

cues.en: And this makes sense from the cognitive load perspective.
cues.zh: 从认知负荷的角度来看，这是合理的。

cues.en: Reading
cues.zh: 阅读

cues.en: expert code with an explanation
cues.zh: 带讲解的专家代码

cues.en: doesn't cost you very much cognitive load. You can just read the code and then, oh, why has this person done this? Oh, there is an explanation right there. I can read it immediately.
cues.zh: 不会花费你太多认知负荷。你可以直接读代码，然后，哦，为什么这个人这样做？哦，那里正好有讲解。我可以立刻读到。

cues.en: So there's lots of cognitive load left
cues.zh: 所以还剩下很多认知负荷

cues.en: to store problem solving chunks to remember, oh, if I have to reverse an array, these are the steps that I would take. I can remember those. They will come in handy in the test.
cues.zh: 要存储解决问题的片段来记忆，哦，如果我要反转一个数组，这些就是我会采取的步骤。我能记住这些。它们在考试中会派上用场。

cues.en: So those
cues.zh: 所以那些

cues.en: two groups didn't even have a difference. They did equally well, so you might as well not have your students
cues.zh: 两组甚至没有差异。他们表现得一样好，所以你干脆别让你的学生

cues.en: write any code because it doesn't make a difference.
cues.zh: 写任何代码，因为写了也没区别。

cues.en: That is spectacular
cues.zh: 这太惊人了

cues.en: given how we currently teach in university
cues.zh: 考虑到我们目前在大学里

cues.en: and in code clubs. Do not have children programming.
cues.zh: 和代码俱乐部里的教学方式。不要让孩子编程。

cues.en: Have them read code and explain them how the code works. So
cues.zh: 让他们阅读代码，并向他们解释代码是如何工作的。所以

cues.en: explicitly teaching strategies
cues.zh: 明确地教授策略

cues.en: really, really works well.
cues.zh: 真的、真的很有效。

cues.en: The third thing that we're currently exploring
cues.zh: 我们目前正在探索的第三件事

cues.en: is assessment, and then specifically assessment in this code club situations.
cues.zh: 是评估，具体来说是在这种代码俱乐部情境下的评估。

cues.en: Because in the same survey I did with my colleague that I talked about earlier,
cues.zh: 因为在我之前提到的和我同事一起做的同一项调查中，

cues.en: we looked at assessment, and only 23%
cues.zh: 我们研究了评估，只有23%

cues.en: of Code Clubs use any form of assessment.
cues.zh: 的代码俱乐部使用任何形式的评估。

cues.en: So it doesn't have to be assessment like you get an A for programming,
cues.zh: 所以不一定是那种编程得A的评估，

cues.en: but just assessment in the sense that the teacher has an idea
cues.zh: 而只是评估，让老师了解

cues.en: of what children have understood. So we do these tiny things now in our code club,
cues.zh: 孩子们理解了些什么。所以我们现在在代码俱乐部里做这些小事情，

cues.en: tiny tests.
cues.zh: 小测试。

cues.en: Which one is a variable? Circle it.
cues.zh: 哪个是变量？圈出来。

cues.en: You want to set the variable points to zero. Which one does that? You can do this in two or three minutes at the end of your club. Just hand out a sheet,
cues.zh: 你想把变量points设为0。哪个能做到？你可以在俱乐部结束时花两三分钟做这个。发一张纸，

cues.en: circle all the things,
cues.zh: 圈出所有东西，

cues.en: and then you'll get an understanding of what kids have memorized.
cues.zh: 然后你就能了解孩子们记住了什么。

cues.en: And there's also research suggesting
cues.zh: 还有研究表明，

cues.en: that if you ask people to remember something,
cues.zh: 如果让人去主动记忆某件事，

cues.en: that will actually strengthen their memory.
cues.zh: 实际上能强化他们的记忆。

cues.en: So having children remember this will increase their ability to recall it in the next week,
cues.zh: 所以让孩子们去记住这些，能提高他们下周回忆起来的能力，

cues.en: plus you will also get an insight of what they know.
cues.zh: 而且你也能掌握他们到底懂了多少。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 然而，

cues.en: of course, here too, there are haters
cues.zh: 当然了，这里也少不了唱反调的人，

cues.en: because haters are everywhere except for running
cues.zh: 因为除了跑步

cues.en: and knitting.
cues.zh: 和织毛衣，杠精无处不在。

cues.en: So people, if I do this talk, I've done this talk a bunch of times at programming conferences,
cues.zh: 我在编程大会上做过好多次这个演讲，

cues.en: and what happens is people come up to me. At this one conference,
cues.zh: 每次都有人来找我交流。有一次大会上，

cues.en: a person came up to me, this was a guy, they're often guys, comes very close,
cues.zh: 有个人走到我面前——是个男的，往往都是男的——凑得特别近，

cues.en: points his finger at me, very close to my nose, says,
cues.zh: 手指几乎戳到了我的鼻子上，说：

cues.en: you're making it look like school.
cues.zh: “你把它搞得像在学校上课一样。”

cues.en: Is is that a bad thing? I mean, school,
cues.zh: 这……这是件坏事吗？我是说，学校，

cues.en: I know there are issues with school, but in general,
cues.zh: 我知道学校存在不少问题，但总体而言，

cues.en: is pretty successful.
cues.zh: 它办得其实挺成功的。

cues.en: Most people can read in most countries where there's education
cues.zh: 在大多数为儿童提供普及教育的国家，

cues.en: for most children, so I don't know.
cues.zh: 绝大多数人都能识字，所以我觉得还好吧。

cues.en: It's not terrible,
cues.zh: 它没那么糟糕，

cues.en: and this anti school is
cues.zh: 而这种反感学校的情绪，

cues.en: also part of our programming culture. We have all these dropouts that are very famous that say, oh, you should don't go to university, you can just start work at a tech company. So
cues.zh: 也是我们编程文化的一部分。我们有那么多名气很大的辍学大佬，宣扬说“别上大学了，直接去科技公司上班吧”。所以

cues.en: against school also fits the whole philosophy of this exploration.
cues.zh: 反对学校也正符合了这种所谓的“自由探索”理念。

cues.en: So people say, it's not fun. Programming should be fun, remember from the books.
cues.zh: 于是大家就说：“这不好玩啊。编程应该是有趣的，就像书里写的那样。”

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是，

cues.en: I have science.
cues.zh: 我有科学依据。

cues.en: It
cues.zh: 有不有趣，

cues.en: actually doesn't matter.
cues.zh: 其实根本不重要。

cues.en: This might be the second most important takeaway of my talk. It doesn't matter if people are having fun for learning.
cues.zh: 这可能是我演讲中第二重要的要点。人们学习时是否觉得有趣，并不重要。

cues.en: I go to this running group
cues.zh: 我参加这个跑步小组

cues.en: every week. So I go to this running group, hello, welcome to running class. We will do 50 push ups.
cues.zh: 每周都去。我去这个跑步小组，大家好，欢迎来上跑步课。我们要做50个俯卧撑。

cues.en: Not fun.
cues.zh: 不好玩。

cues.en: You know what's fun? Lying on my couch watching Netflix and eating potato chips.
cues.zh: 你知道什么好玩吗？躺在沙发上刷Netflix，吃薯片。

cues.en: Fun.
cues.zh: 好玩。

cues.en: 50 push ups, not fun.
cues.zh: 50个俯卧撑，不好玩。

cues.en: So why do I do this? Because I know it will make me stronger, it will make me quicker. The same is true for learning. Children
cues.zh: 那我为什么还要做？因为我知道这会让我更强壮、更敏捷。学习也是一样。孩子们

cues.en: know that learning is no fun.
cues.zh: 知道学习不好玩。

cues.en: Children already, when they come into elementary school, have learned to walk and they fell all the time. Not fun. Still they went through it. They may have learned to ride a bike. They fell all the time. Not fun.
cues.zh: 孩子们进小学时，早就学会了走路，他们一路都在摔跤。不好玩。但他们还是熬过来了。他们可能还学会了骑自行车。一路都在摔跤。不好玩。

cues.en: Everyone knows that learning isn't necessarily fun. Learning is hard work, but still adults think that motivation
cues.zh: 大家都知道学习未必好玩。学习是苦差事，但成年人还是以为动机

cues.en: somehow leads to skill, that if children are having fun and they really want to learn, that they will learn. This is not true.
cues.zh: somehow能带来技能，以为只要孩子觉得好玩、真心想学，就一定能学会。这不对。

cues.en: There is a relation, but it actually more goes the other way around.
cues.zh: 两者有关系，但其实是反过来的。

cues.en: If children are learning, if they are acquiring skill,
cues.zh: 如果孩子们在学，在掌握技能，

cues.en: they will be motivated.
cues.zh: 他们自然会有动力。

cues.en: I did the 50 push ups. Hey, I broke my personal record. Yes, this is working. I will do more.
cues.zh: 我做完了50个俯卧撑。嘿，我破了个人纪录。对，这有效。我要做更多。

cues.en: Children know this. So this whole learning should be fun. We should probably stop saying it because it's very much about
cues.zh: 孩子们懂这个。所以“学习应该好玩”这句话，我们大概该别再说了，因为关键其实是

cues.en: realizing your learning, realizing your advancing, and that will bring the motivation and not the other way around.
cues.zh: 意识到自己在学、在进步，这才会带来动力，而不是反过来。

cues.en: So that's more or less everything I wanted to share with you, but let me take this opportunity to summarize my talk in like two minutes I have left, because some people came in late and it's early and you might be jet lagged. So let me give you a second chance to get the gist of this whole talk.
cues.zh: 我想分享的内容大概就这些了。不过趁最后还剩两分钟，我来给大家做个总结，毕竟有人来晚了，时间又早，大家可能还有时差。所以我再给大家一次机会，快速掌握整个演讲的要点。

cues.en: First of all,
cues.zh: 首先，

cues.en: don't be these people.
cues.zh: 别成为这种人。

cues.en: Do not be these people. Don't say this is not real programming because it's not necessary. We should be like runners. Everyone should like programming,
cues.zh: 千万别成为这种人。不要说什么“这根本不是真正的编程”，完全没必要。我们应该像跑步爱好者一样，人人都应该喜欢编程，

cues.en: and everyone should be a programmer. So please don't be these people, and and don't allow these people in too much.
cues.zh: 人人都能成为程序员。所以请不要做这种人，也别给这种言论太多市场。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 不过，

cues.en: before you do that, I'm actually together with Laura, the CSS algorithms lady, I'm running a little online survey.
cues.zh: 在此之前，我和 Laura——就是讲 CSS 算法的那位女士——其实正在搞一个小型的在线问卷。

cues.en: So for once, before you never do it again anymore,
cues.zh: 所以就破例这一次，在以后彻底不再划分之前，

cues.en: we would actually like your opinion on how you see programming languages on the spectrum of least to most programming.
cues.zh: 我们想了解一下你的看法：在从“最不像编程”到“最硬核编程”的区间里，你会如何给各种编程语言排序。

cues.en: So we made this web app where you can put your languages.
cues.zh: 于是我们做了这个 Web 应用，你可以把各门语言放进去排个序。

cues.en: You can do this in secret, and you know, no one looks at you while you're doing it.
cues.zh: 你可以悄悄填，放心，填的时候没人会看着你。

cues.en: Because if we wanna battle this together,
cues.zh: 因为如果我们想一起扭转这种偏见，

cues.en: we should also understand
cues.zh: 就得先弄清楚，

cues.en: what is seen as most and least programming. And we have this open text box also because we want to understand
cues.zh: 大家眼里到底什么才算“最编程”，什么算“最不编程”。我们还留了一个开放文本框，也是想了解

cues.en: why do you think this? Is it about testing type systems, syntax?
cues.zh: 你为什么会这么想？是因为测试、类型系统，还是语法？

cues.en: We want to understand this culture because understanding it will be a more effective way to change it than me saying, don't be like that. So please
cues.zh: 我们想理解这种文化，因为比起我在这干说“别这样”，深入理解才能更有效地改变它。所以，

cues.en: don't say it but. Fill out our survey. This is a link. I will also have it at all the end, all the way at the end of my talk, the same link, so you don't need to do it right now. I will show it at the end as well. It will be very helpful for us if you share this link, if you fill it out, because we want to get this...
cues.zh: 先别急着下定论，来填下我们的问卷吧。这是链接。演讲最后我还会再放一次这个链接，所以不用现在急着填，我待会儿还会展示。如果大家能填一下并帮忙转发这个链接，对我们会有非常大的帮助，因为我们想……

cues.en: Understand this vibe of what the community believes about programming.
cues.zh: 理解一下社区对编程的这种观念氛围。

cues.en: So this talk was about how to teach programming because I tried it in a bad way, and it was not very enjoyable for me or the kids,
cues.zh: 所以这次演讲是关于如何教编程的，因为我试过一种糟糕的方式，对我或孩子们来说都不太愉快，

cues.en: mainly because I was thinking of how I learned programming,
cues.zh: 主要是因为我当时想的是自己是怎么学编程的，

cues.en: which is how many people learn programming, and that was without a teacher.
cues.zh: 这也是很多人学编程的方式，那就是没有老师。

cues.en: And this culture of not having a teacher is very visible in programming books and online materials that all say, just have some fun.
cues.zh: 这种没有老师的文化在编程书和在线资料中非常明显，它们都说，就随便玩玩吧。

cues.en: Probably this is also amplified by the history of programming education
cues.zh: 这可能也被编程教育的历史所放大

cues.en: because the creator of programming education for children very much believed that explaining was a bad thing, but now we know that explaining actually is a good thing, and there's ample research in all sorts of field showing that
cues.zh: 因为儿童编程教育的创始者非常相信讲解是件坏事，但现在我们知道讲解其实是件好事，而且各个领域都有大量研究表明

cues.en: if you want children to understand stuff, you should explain them. And this is what we are exploring now in my research group where we're looking into having children read aloud,
cues.zh: 如果你想让孩子们理解东西，就应该给他们讲解。这正是我们研究组现在在探索的，我们在研究让孩子朗读，

cues.en: explicitly teaching them how to solve problems, and explicitly
cues.zh: 明确教他们如何解决问题，并且明确地

cues.en: using assessment also in out of school programs.
cues.zh: 在校外项目中也使用评估。
